changes.evidence: A long independent line runs beneath multiplicité, crossing the descending p but continuing below the other letters. H does not mark the visible underline.
Between donc and ce is a separate word with a low loop, tall looped d and long e return. The extra de is written and is retained without grammatical normalization.

The cancelled first letter is a large capital O with an upright oval loop, followed by the low n run beneath the cancelling stroke. The replacement et is written above it. This supports capital On rather than the lower-case ou in H.
The live word has the initial r/e, the large descending g loop, a/r, tall d, and the compressed o/n/s ending. No independent on precedes it, and the ending is not era.
At the head of the line is the small alpha followed directly by fixé and a comma. There is no pour before it and no insertion leader or separate raised placement for this phrase.
The word has two looped d forms, low intervening vowels, an i-dot, a crossed t and the final e return, followed by a separate comma. These strokes do not spell disons.

Between comme and pour is the longer t-a-n-t-o-t sequence: an initial tall t, the extended low middle, another raised/crossed member, and a terminal t. It is longer than tout. The crop clips part of the upper ascenders, so the circumflex is not treated as absent; the accent remains explicitly uncertain and the second-reading box extends upward.

The ending has a tall crossed f-like form with a long descending return. It is heavily retraced and crossed below the line, so the final state is not fully recoverable. Relatif remains the preferred reading, with relative retained; no independent extra word is supplied for H’s trailing illegible placeholder.
After the U in the phrase ou ... sur un, the subscript S is tall and vertically extended, with a long descending curved body and lower hook. It has the capital S shape, followed by a smaller alpha.

The word before the cancellation ends in a small downward return after the long e stroke, supporting the final s of des. The abbreviation that follows is separately read as pt.; the written determiner is not normalized to match it.

The tall t and i-dot remain visible, but the horizontal cancellation covers most of the following low letters. A low final trace is compatible with plural sections, but a separate final s cannot be established securely. C’s plural is retained as the preferred reading and H’s singular as an alternative.
The live abbreviation has one p descender, a small raised crossed t and a separate low point. There is no intervening s between t and the point.
The next manuscript row begins directly with the short rat. and then sur k(s_alpha). There is no spelled-out rationnel or intervening on a un pt. between the preceding live pt. and this rat.
The main letter after de has two tall arms joined by an open lower basin: U, not the crossing diagonals of X. Its small subscript is retraced; the s/S case remains unresolved.
After the dash are two low separated word groups with a detached apostrophe over the latter. They read on n’a, not the dotted abbreviation i.e.
The following row begins with a q loop and long descender, followed by the low u, apostrophe and un. The initial qu’ is written.
After pt are the small à, a tall l with an apostrophe, and the i/n/f/i/n/i run with a prominent f descender and separate i-dots. These are the written words à l’infini before the point formula.
The point formula ends with its comma, and the next base-text row starts rat sur k_alpha. No second i.e. qui est à l’infini clause is written there; the actual à l’infini occurs before the formula.
The small t after r/a has its cross-stroke but no separate following abbreviation point before sur. The period farther right belongs after the field expression, not after rat.

changes.h: maintenant rat. ... Mais on dispose d’un
changes.evidence: Maintenant is written above the space preceding d’un. Its long curved leader descends into that exact gap after dispose. It does not attach before rat on the preceding row.

The short horizontal stroke at façon crosses the f stem as that letter’s own crossbar. It does not run across de or independently cancel the whole phrase; the rest of façon remains ordinary live writing.
The bottom-left margin has a separate faint 9 with descending tail followed by the two lobes of 3.

marks.evidence: The final tall crossed form and descender favor f, but heavy retracing and crossing beneath the line prevent a secure final-state decision. The existing alternatives remain.
The main U is clear; the small subscript before alpha is overworked and does not securely resolve lowercase s against capital S. Both C alternatives remain.

The left k and lower alpha are visible, but a dense retraced body and tiny separate trace remain to the right. Their relation to an overwritten older form is not clear, so the whole expression stays doubtful.

notes:
This leaf first identifies the quantity discussed in the preceding continuation with the multiplicity along a divisor component D_alpha. It then asks what happens for points on the union of those components, fixes one alpha, and describes an extension attached to the generic point of that component and a suitable open subset. In this situation the text says that there are no longer rational points of the generic curve of the earlier kind, but a rational point at infinity i_alpha; it then refers to a subgroup L_i of pi attached to that point in an essentially canonical fashion. The final comma continues the discussion. This summarizes the page’s statements without asserting that they have been proved or checked.
Visual review: the whole sheet and both full-resolution halves were viewed once. The first bottom-half tool call failed before displaying the image; the successful retry was the single actual bottom-half view. Every word, formula, abbreviation, index, sign, cancellation, insertion and underline was compared against both witnesses. Fifteen saved crops were inspected once, with no recropping. The crops use the original boxes recorded here, grayscale autocontrast, LANCZOS resizing to 2200 pixels width and sharpening. No OCR, text recognition, external research, or other leaf was consulted. The sheet contains twenty prose rows including the compressed last row, no diagram or drawing, no visible author page number at its head, and the separate folio 93 at bottom left.
Reading decisions: C is supported for the extra de after donc, capital cancelled On with inserted et, regardons, inline alpha fixé without pour, déduite, the capital S in the earlier U_Salpha, and the later words on n’a qu’un pt à l’infini. Multiplicité is underlined. The live abbreviation before rat. is pt., not C’s pts.; no s lies between the small raised t and its following point. Des is retained as written. The deleted sections/section remains uncertain under its strike. The point at infinity formula and the curved leader place maintenant after dispose, not before rat. The later rat has no abbreviation point. De façon remains live: the local horizontal stroke belongs to the f crossbar rather than a phrase-wide cancellation.
The adjective ending remains relatif|relative because its f-like descender is heavily retraced. In the later U expression, U itself is clear against H’s X, but the s/S subscript remains overworked. The k_alpha expression retains its doubt because the dense right-side retracing and small trace cannot be separated confidently from the visible k and lower alpha. The long word after comme is tantot rather than tout; the circumflex is retained as the preferred possibility, but its exact accent state remains uncertain because the crop clips part of the upper ascenders. Its anonymous second-reading box extends upward beyond the crop so this can be checked without assuming an accent absent. The point-at-infinity second box likewise extends upward to include the complete upper part of the formula. In that box maintenant is shown on its separate physical line; its actual attachment after dispose is given in the insertion box and full draft. No author question mark is added. Font/macro conventions such as E versus mathcal E are not counted as reading changes.
Mathematical checks: no independent proof, computation, mathematical use or refutation was performed. The content summary above describes the manuscript, and the stroke comparisons are visual checks only. check_events remains empty. No compilation was performed.
